before.html:
Question 1

Given that the horizontal asymptote of the function f(x)=24x3−12cx3−15x2 is y=−13, find the value of c.

a
 4
b
 −36
c
 14
d
 −4
e
 −14

decision.explanation: The horizontal asymptote is the ratio of leading coefficients: 24/(2c)=12/c. Setting 12/c=-1/3 gives c=-36.

history.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{3}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{24{x}^{3}-1}{2c{x}^{3}-15{x}^{2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{24{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{2c{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{15{x}^{2}}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(24-\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})}{(2c-\frac{15}{x})} \\  & =\frac{24-0}{2c-0} \\  & =\frac{12}{c}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{12}{c} & =-\frac{1}{3} \\ c & =-36.\end{aligned}
$$
history.html:

Therefore, 12c=−13c=−36.

Question 3
A scientific calculator is required to answer the following question.
Expressed in ascending order in degrees, rounded to the nearest integer, the solutions to the equation −csc⁡x=7+2csc⁡x for 0∘≤x<360∘, are
x≈
∘,x≈
∘.

decision.explanation: The worked solution confirms sin(x)=-3/7. Its solutions in the required interval are approximately 205.377° and 334.623°, so ascending order and rounding give 205 and 335. The displayed submission of 25 for the first field is incorrect because sine is positive at 25°.

history.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, isolating $\operatorname{csc}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{csc}⁡x & =7+2\operatorname{csc}⁡x \\ -3\operatorname{csc}⁡x & =7 \\ \operatorname{csc}⁡x & =-\frac{7}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that $\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}.$ Therefore, the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡x=-\frac{3}{7}.
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-\frac{3}{7})=(-25.376\,933…)^{∘}≈-{25.377}^{∘}
$$

This value is outside the required domain. To get a value inside the range, we add ${360}^{∘}:$

$$
{x}_{1}=-{25.377}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}={334.623}^{∘}
$$

So,  our first solution is ${x}_{1}={334.623}^{∘}.$

Our first solution lies in the fourth quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={25.377}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={25.377}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062614/assets/2358d2c829f52ba8727afc10a609f923ca441bb55dc398cda78c619454f6eac5.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={180}^{∘}+{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={180}^{∘}+{25.377}^{∘} \\  & ={205.377}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

So, in ascending order, rounded to the nearest integer, the solutions are 

$$
x≈{205}^{∘},\,x≈{335}^{∘}.
$$

So, our first solution is x1=334.623∘.

before.html:
Question 4
Given a curve x=−5y+y2, what is the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point (−4,1)?
y=

decision.explanation: Differentiating with respect to y gives dx/dy=5/y^2+2y. At y=1, dx/dy=7, so the tangent slope is dy/dx=1/7. Thus y-1=(x+4)/7, giving y=(x+11)/7.

history.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(-\frac{5}{y}+{y}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(-5{y}^{-1}+{y}^{2}) \\  & =-5\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-1})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2}) \\  & =-5(-{y}^{-2})+2y \\  & =2y+5{y}^{-2} \\  & =2y+\frac{5}{{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2{y}^{3}+5}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{{y}^{2}}{2{y}^{3}+5}.
$$

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $(-4,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(-4,1)} \\  & =\frac{{1}^{2}}{2(1)^{3}+5} \\  & =\frac{1}{2+5} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot (x-(-4)) \\ y & =\frac{1}{7}x+\frac{4}{7}+1 \\ y & =\frac{1}{7}x+\frac{11}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of dxdy, we get

dydx=(dxdy)−1=y22y3+5.

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point (−4,1) is m=dydx|(x,y)=(−4,1)=122(1)3+5=12+5=17.

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get y−y1=m(x−x1)y−1=17⋅(x−(−4))y=17x+47+1y=17x+117.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of a Tangent Line Using dx/dy
content.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(-\frac{5}{y}+{y}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(-5{y}^{-1}+{y}^{2}) \\  & =-5\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-1})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2}) \\  & =-5(-{y}^{-2})+2y \\  & =2y+5{y}^{-2} \\  & =2y+\frac{5}{{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2{y}^{3}+5}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{{y}^{2}}{2{y}^{3}+5}.
$$

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $(-4,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(-4,1)} \\  & =\frac{{1}^{2}}{2(1)^{3}+5} \\  & =\frac{1}{2+5} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot (x-(-4)) \\ y & =\frac{1}{7}x+\frac{4}{7}+1 \\ y & =\frac{1}{7}x+\frac{11}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

history.worked_solution:
The first three terms of the binomial expansion for $(1+x)^{n}$ are given by

$$
(1+x)^{n}=1+nx+\frac{n(n-1)}{2!}{x}^{2}+⋯.
$$

By substituting $x=-5t$ and $n=7$ into the above formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1-5t)}^{7} & =1+7\cdot (-5t)+\frac{7(7-1)}{2!}\cdot (-5t)^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1-35t+\frac{7\cdot 6}{2}\cdot 25{t}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1-35t+21\cdot 25{t}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1-35t+525{t}^{2}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$
